content.question: To add a new screen in Android Studio, which folder do you right-click on to start the process?
content.explanation: To add a new screen, you expand the kotlin+java folder and always right-click on the first sub-folder inside it, then navigate to New → Activity.
hints: The kotlin+java folder contains three sub-folders.
You should always go with the first one.
Right-clicking it reveals options including New.

content.question: Which menu option chain correctly leads to adding a new Activity screen in Android Studio?

options.text: Right-click → New → Activity → Empty Views Activity

content.explanation: The correct path is right-click → New → Activity → Empty Views Activity, which is the same option used when the project was first created.
hints: You hover over 'New' to see sub-options.
The term 'Activity' is used for screens in Android.
Empty Views Activity was used when the project was first set up.

content.question: When you add a second Activity named 'MainActivityTwo', which two files are automatically generated?
content.explanation: Android Studio generates a Kotlin class file (MainActivityTwo.kt) under kotlin+java and an XML layout file (activity_main_two.xml) under the layout folder.
hints: One file goes into kotlin+java and one goes into the layout folder.
The XML layout file name uses underscores instead of camel case.
The Kotlin class retains the camel case naming.

content.question: Which component should you use when you want to display an image in an Android layout?
content.explanation: ImageView is the component dedicated to displaying images in an Android layout.
hints: The name of the component directly describes its purpose.
It is different from TextView which is for text.
Type 'image' in the XML editor and it appears as the first suggestion.

content.question: What is the mandatory attribute of ImageView that defines where its image comes from?
content.explanation: The android:src attribute is mandatory for ImageView. It stands for 'source' and defines the image to display.
hints: The attribute name is a short word meaning where something originates.
'src' is short for 'source'.
Just like TextView has android:text, ImageView has this mandatory attribute.

content.question: Where are images typically stored in an Android project?
content.explanation: Images are typically stored in the drawable folder inside the res (resources) directory of an Android project.
hints: The folder name literally describes its contents.
It is located inside the res directory.
To access it: app → res → drawable.

content.question: What syntax is used in the android:src attribute to point to an image inside the drawable folder?
content.explanation: The @ symbol is used to reference resources. @drawable/imagename tells Android to go into the drawable folder and find the image with that name.
hints: The @ symbol locates a resource directory.
After the directory name comes a forward slash and then the image name.
The format is: @folder/name.

content.question: Which two images are available in the drawable folder by default when a new Android project is created?
content.explanation: Android Studio provides ic_launcher_foreground and ic_launcher_background as default drawable images in every new project.
hints: Both names start with 'ic_launcher_'.
One is the foreground layer and one is the background layer.
These are the Android launcher icon components.

content.question: What is the first method to add a custom external image into the drawable folder?

options.text: Type the image URL directly into the SRC attribute
Right-click the drawable folder → Open in Finder/Explorer → copy the image in
Use the Android Studio image importer from the File menu
Paste the image path into the XML file manually

content.explanation: The first method is to right-click the drawable folder, choose Open in Finder (Mac) or Show in Explorer (Windows), then copy and paste the image file directly into that folder.
hints: This method uses the file system to copy the image.
On Mac you get Finder; on Windows you get Explorer.
After copying, the image appears in Android Studio without any refresh.

content.question: What is the second method to add a custom image into the drawable folder in Android Studio?

options.text: Drag and drop the image file directly onto the drawable folder in the project panel
Place the image in the layout folder instead
Compress the image into a ZIP file and import it

content.explanation: The second method is to drag and drop the image file directly onto the drawable folder in the Android Studio project panel. A refactor dialog appears; accept it and the image is added.
hints: This method does not require opening the file system.
A dialog box with a 'Refactor' option appears when you drop the file.
It is faster and more convenient than the first method.

content.question: What is the rule for naming image files placed in the drawable folder?

options.text: Names must be in ALL CAPS
Names must be in all lowercase characters
Names can contain any mix of uppercase and lowercase
Names must start with a capital letter

content.explanation: Image file names in the drawable folder must use only lowercase characters. Using uppercase letters causes errors in Android Studio.
hints: Capital letters in the name trigger error indicators in the editor.
The instructor demonstrated this by deliberately using uppercase and showing the error.
Always rename files to lowercase before placing them in the drawable folder.

content.question: What is the shortcut key to rename a file in Android Studio using the Refactor menu?
content.explanation: To rename a file in Android Studio, right-click → Refactor → Rename, or use the shortcut Shift + F6.
hints: The shortcut uses both a modifier key and a function key.
It is found under the Refactor context menu.
Shift + F6 opens the rename dialog directly.

content.question: What does the android:gravity attribute do for a TextView?

options.text: It moves the entire TextView to a different position on the screen
It aligns the text content within the TextView box
It increases the font weight of the text

content.explanation: android:gravity aligns the text content within the boundaries of the TextView widget. For example, center gravity places the text in the middle of the TextView box.
hints: Gravity controls position of content inside the view, not the view itself.
Setting it to 'center' places text in the center of the box.
The definition of gravity in Android is 'alignment', not physical gravity.

content.question: Which attribute controls the font size of the text in a TextView?
content.explanation: android:textSize controls the font size of the text displayed in a TextView. You can set it to a value like 30sp.
hints: The attribute name directly combines 'text' and 'size'.
Common units for text size are sp (scale-independent pixels).
The instructor set it to 30sp in the demonstration.

content.question: Which attribute is used to make text bold or italic in a TextView?
content.explanation: android:textStyle sets the style of the text. Accepted values are bold, italic, normal, and bold|italic.
hints: Style refers to the visual weight and slant of text.
The valid values include bold, italic, and normal.
You can combine bold and italic using the pipe character.

content.question: Which attribute changes the color of the text in a TextView?
content.explanation: android:textColor sets the color of the text in a TextView. You can use color names like 'black' or hex color codes.
hints: The attribute combines 'text' and 'color'.
You can search 'color' in the XML editor to find it quickly.
It accepts color names like 'black' as well as hex values.

content.question: Where can a developer find the full list of available attributes for a TextView?

options.text: Only in the Android Studio XML autocomplete
In the TextView API reference on Android's official Google documentation
Only in paid Android developer courses
In the Android emulator settings menu

content.explanation: The full list of TextView attributes is available in the official TextView API reference on Google's Android developer documentation website.
hints: The instructor searched for 'textview' in a browser to find it.
It is the first result and is labeled 'TextView API reference'.
The official documentation is free and accessible at any time.

content.question: When Android Studio renames a file that is already referenced in the XML, what happens to the reference?

options.text: The reference breaks and must be manually updated
Android Studio automatically updates the reference everywhere it is used
The old file is duplicated under the new name

content.explanation: When you rename a file via Refactor → Rename in Android Studio, it automatically updates all references to that file throughout the project.
hints: The instructor demonstrated renaming 'unnamed' and the XML reference updated automatically.
This is the advantage of using Refactor → Rename over simple file renaming.
Android Studio's refactoring tools handle all dependency updates.

content.question: After adding an image file to the drawable folder, do you need to refresh Android Studio to see it?

options.text: Yes, you must restart Android Studio
Yes, you must click the Sync Project button
No, the image appears automatically without any refresh

content.explanation: Once an image is placed inside the drawable folder, it appears in Android Studio automatically without needing a manual refresh or restart.
hints: The instructor explicitly stated this point during the demonstration.
No extra steps are required after placing the file in the folder.
Android Studio monitors the folder and updates in real time.

content.question: What does the gravity value 'center' do to text inside a TextView that has a width of 250dp and height of 60dp?

options.text: It moves the entire TextView to the center of the screen
It places the text in the horizontal and vertical center of the 250dp × 60dp box
It increases the text size to fill the box

content.explanation: Setting android:gravity to 'center' positions the text content in the center of the TextView's own bounding box, not on the screen.
hints: Gravity affects content inside the view, not the view's position.
The instructor used it to fix text that was stuck in the top-left of the box.
The TextView box dimensions stay the same; only the text position changes.
